opening: Our React forms are built with react-hook-form (current main branch): useForm with register, setValue, reset, formState and the form's submit handler (called with an onValid and an onInvalid callback), validate rules or a resolver, and field arrays for lists of rows, some with rules of their own on the array. We found three problems.

requirements.m01: When validation itself throws during a submit, the form never leaves the submitting state. If a validate rule, the resolver or the onInvalid callback throws, synchronously or by returning a rejected promise, the promise of the submit must reject with exactly the thrown value (a falsy value such as 0 included), and formState must settle as if no submit had happened: isSubmitting false, isSubmitted false, isSubmitSuccessful false and submitCount 0. formState.errors keeps what validation found before the exception: the field's required error (type 'required', message 'required') when onInvalid throws after a required field failed, and {} when the resolver or the validate rule throws. A submit whose onValid callback throws keeps today's result: isSubmitting false, isSubmitted true, isSubmitSuccessful false and submitCount 1. When reset() is called while a submit still waits for the resolver, subscribers to isSubmitting are told at once that isSubmitting is false (with isSubmitted false, isSubmitSuccessful false and submitCount 0); when the resolver then rejects, the submit promise rejects with that error, no further form state is published, and neither onValid nor onInvalid is called.
requirements.m02: setValue on an object that contains a field array updates the values but not the rendered rows. With defaultValues { section: { title: '', items } }, a field array on 'section.items' and one input registered per row as section.items.${index}.value, calling setValue('section', { title: 'title', items: [...] }) leaves the old rows on screen although getValues('section.items') already returns the new ones. The rendered rows must show exactly the new values, with or without rules on the field array: with rules { required: true }, ['a'] set to ['x', 'y', 'z'], an empty array set to ['x', 'y', 'z'], and ['a', 'b', 'c'] set to ['z']; without rules, an empty array set to ['x', 'y']. Writing the same rows again (['a'] to ['a']) keeps the one row. With the rules { maxLength: { value: 2, message: 'at most 2 rows' } } and setValue('section', { title: 'title', items: [x, y, z rows] }, { shouldValidate: true }), the error message 'at most 2 rows' is shown and 3 rows are rendered. A nested field array behaves the same: with defaultValues { rows: [{ name: 'row', tags: [] }] }, a field array on 'rows' and a component with a field array on 'rows.0.tags' (one input per tag, registered as rows.0.tags.${index}.label), setValue('rows.0', { name: 'row', tags: [{ label: 'one' }, { label: 'two' }] }) must render two tag inputs, the second with the value 'two'.
requirements.m03: After reset(), a field array stops enforcing the rules given for the array itself when those rules are the same object on every render (a constant, as most of our forms define them). With a field array on 'items' and rules { required: 'add an item' } on defaultValues { items: [] }, calling reset() and then submitting calls onValid instead of showing 'add an item'; the same happens inside React.StrictMode and with reset(undefined, { keepValues: true }). formState.isValid is false before the reset and must stay false after it. With rules { minLength: { value: 2, message: 'add two items' } }, defaultValues { items: [{ value: 'a' }] } and reset({ items: [{ value: 'b' }] }), the submit must show 'add two items' and not call onValid; the same when the form's values prop changes from { items: [{ value: 'a' }] } to { items: [{ value: 'b' }] }. Rows that meet the rules still submit after a reset: with two rows and minLength 2, reset() then submit calls onValid once and shows no error.
